before: You pay to retire the claim before it spreads. {{sibling}} is relieved; your trust in that relief is sharply reduced.
after: The lender cancels the claim. {{sibling}} offers to sign a note of gratitude; you suggest leaving the pen where it is.

before: You lose some household wealth but gain a grateful neighbour. The lower shelves produce fewer requests for help.
after: {{other}} takes the ladder home permanently. You lower the shelves and stop receiving requests to borrow your furniture’s only means of escape.

before: You pay for the roof repair. The household’s shelter improves and supper no longer requires moving the bowls between drops.
after: The bowls return to holding supper instead of rain. The repairer leaves with your money and, at last, the household’s weather.

before: You preserve your purse while damp consumes part of the household’s food and furnishings. The economy is mostly imaginary.
after: You move the bowls and keep the coin. The damp eats part of the stores without once presenting an estimate.

before: You pay restitution and restore your child’s trust. The explanation is harder than the payment.
after: You return the goods and pay the loss. {{child}} watches you admit the lesson before asking whether adults have to practise it too.

before: You refuse the false testimony. {{other}} loses trust in your usefulness; your own legal record remains untouched.
after: {{other}} folds the proposed testimony. Your memory has failed to become useful, an imperfection they find very difficult to forgive.

before: You accept a promise of payment and acquire a real perjury charge. The promised money is still only a promise.
after: The clerk records your oath and asks a second question. {{other}} remembers promising payment rather less clearly than you remember promising to have been there.

before: You pay for discretion and dubious eyesight. {{other}} is pleased to find affection has a solvent friend.
after: {{other}} accepts payment for having seen less. The bill is exceptionally legible for work conducted in such poor light.

before: You pay for a little hospitality and the humiliation passes without an audience. {{other}} remembers the door that actually opened.
after: You pay for a dry place to wait and close the door on the audience. {{other}} discovers that a little hospitality travels farther than the verse.

before: You pay for the visit and improve the food reserve. {{spouse}} appreciates generosity that does not arrive attached to a complaint.
after: The food is bought before the visit becomes an argument. {{spouse}} welcomes a contribution that has not brought its own speech.

before: You pay seven gold for sunlight you were not using. {{other}} accepts the money without conceding the existence of clouds.
after: {{other}} accepts seven gold for the shade. A cloud passes over the transaction without paying anything.

before: You keep your arm unmarked and disappoint {{other}}. It is an exceptionally affordable disappointment.
after: {{other}} improves the offer, apparently believing your skin has failed to understand the first price. Your arm leaves the negotiation unchanged.

before: You preserve the evidence and anger {{other}}. Your reputation improves for resisting a surprisingly domestic form of fraud.
after: The stain stays on the cloth and out of the wash. {{other}} calls this an unreasonable use of cleanliness as evidence.

before: You preserve your strength at the cost of your cellmate’s affection. The list remains remarkably well fed.
after: You eat your share in full. {{other}} watches the bowl empty with an expression that will be present at the next division.

before: You refuse the story and retain a clear legal record. {{other}} resents the accuracy of your memory.
after: {{other}} asks whether you are quite certain you remember correctly. You remain inconveniently certain.

before: You improve your public standing by surrendering the plan. {{other}} now regards you as a rival; your cell door is still locked.
after: The gaoler takes the plan and examines the drawing. {{other}} now regards you as a rival; the drawing has still opened more conversation than doors.

before: You pay the disputed amount without creating a criminal conviction. The receipt is more certain than the accusation ever was.
after: The disputed fine is paid and a receipt supplied. {{other}} has settled the amount without once managing to establish the offence.

before: You refuse blind involvement in the smuggling. {{other}} withdraws the offer and a little of their goodwill.
after: You ask to inspect the contents. {{other}} withdraws both the offer and the claim that curiosity is a virtue.

before: You pay for a statement worth reading aloud. Your reputation improves; the document does not pardon a single offence.
after: The clerk produces a statement worth reading. {{other}} looks relieved until you insist on reading the useful part aloud too.

before: You gain no automatic release. Instead, you add a false-testimony charge to the record and make {{other}} party to a dangerous confidence.
after: The clerk adds your false statement to the file. {{other}} has supplied an entirely genuine reason for both of you to be questioned again.

before: You pay for a truthful petition and gain public standing. The prison sentence continues while the complaint is considered.
after: Your petition is lodged and receipted. {{other}} agrees that paper travels remarkably well through a door neither of you can open.

before: You gain practical experience by risking the appearance of not already knowing everything. {{other}} watches you put down the rulebook.
after: You put down the rulebook and try the joint. {{other}} has the kindness not to mention how long the rulebook delayed this discovery.

before: You pay the booking fee and keep the capital out of the river. {{other}} dislikes your caution until it rains harder.
after: The booking fee is lost; the goods remain dry. {{other}} begins to respect your caution at exactly the rate the rain increases.

before: You pay for better protection and gain trading experience without inventing a guaranteed profit. {{other}} trusts your terms more than the forecast.
after: The covering is paid for and the terms recorded. {{other}} finds a contract rather less responsive to the weather than a promise.

before: You improve your working judgement and lose a little of {{other}}’s enthusiasm. Silence turns out to have conditions.
after: {{other}} reads the limits on “silent” twice. The second reading is noticeably quieter.

before: You refuse damaged goods and gain experience. {{other}} says you are missing an opportunity; the moths are already taking theirs.
after: {{other}} says you are missing an opportunity. A moth leaves the sample at that moment, having taken its share already.

before: You pay for the damaged lot and gain craft experience sorting what can be used. No miraculous resale profit arrives with it.
after: You buy the usable remnants and sort the damage honestly. {{other}} objects to your description chiefly because it explains the price.

before: You gain standing with neighbouring households and experience managing rents. {{other}} resents being asked to price the impossible.
after: The neighbours sign your petition. {{other}} is asked to explain which part of the impossible eel can be accepted in payment.

before: You spend your rest on the repair and gain husbandry experience. The field’s prospects improve without altering the calendar.
after: You repair the plough during the rest day. {{other}} praises the work after confirming that admiration does not count as joining it.

before: You gain faith and lose some work performance. {{other}} approves of a sacrifice you are both able to measure.
after: The field waits and you keep the observance. {{other}} approves a sacrifice for which the accounts can supply an exact measure.

before: You keep the text honest and improve your professional standing. {{other}} pays you in displeasure rather than praise.
after: You restore “not”. {{other}} discovers that the smallest word on the page has become the largest difficulty in the case.

before: You gain twelve gold and a forgery charge. One missing word has found a remarkably large place in the evidence.
after: Twelve gold buys one absent word. The clerk makes room for it again beneath the heading for forgery.

before: You gain experience from a slower, sounder inquiry. {{other}} must wait for a result that can survive being read twice.
after: You compare the hands, dates and seals. {{other}} has to wait for an answer capable of surviving a second copy.

before: You improve your professional performance by refusing to diagnose a date. {{other}} trusts your work more than your convenience.
after: You insist on examining a person rather than a date. {{other}} looks offended until asked which one they would prefer treated.

before: You keep your record clean and lose a little client affection. The unexamined patient remains unexamined, whatever the letter wanted.
after: The convenient certificate remains unsigned. {{other}} must find a physician whose memory can be hired separately from their eyes.

before: You gain experience and improve the client’s trust without inventing a diagnosis. The jar is now a problem of disposal rather than medicine.
after: You label the jar and separate it from the diagnosis. {{other}} admits the patient may require more attention than the container.

before: You preserve your freedom and lose the patron’s favour. The unfinished rhyme is an unusually safe silence.
after: The patron takes back the underlined verse. For once your safest line is the one nobody will hear you recite.

before: You improve your performance and gain the company’s respect. {{other}} has to find a buyer with less demanding feet.
after: The company inspects the boots and starts laughing with both feet. {{other}} seeks a buyer less committed to having a left and a right.

before: You gain practical experience and lose some health to the long repair. The men can march, though no one praises the shape.
after: You work through the repair with sore hands. The men can march; praise is confined to the admirable discovery of two directions.

before: You improve your working judgement and the band’s trust. Arithmetic proves useful even in an irregular profession.
after: You remove the goods nobody has stolen yet. {{other}} concedes that an honest account is a useful precaution in a dishonest profession.

before: You gain favour and record a real fourteen-gold obligation. The debt is the first item in the account to become entirely genuine.
after: The band approves the advance. Fourteen gold is entered as your obligation, the first entirely genuine item on the page.

before: You gain ten gold and acquire a feud with {{other}}. An outlaw’s account can be corrected without consulting a court.
after: You take ten gold. {{other}} corrects the account without a clerk, beginning with a very clear description of you.

before: You pay for compensation and improve your family’s reputation for candour. {{other}} is relieved that the bird’s final journey need not become a border dispute.
after: The compensation is paid. {{other}} accepts an honest account of the bird’s final journey, while the cook quietly removes the remaining wing.

before: You preserve an honest account and gain Crown standing. {{other}} loses some affection for the witness who refused to improve the story.
after: You insist on an accurate account. {{other}} signs it with the expression of someone being asked to recognise dinner as a diplomatic document.

before: You gain favour with {{other}} at a small cost to your own dignity. The portrait accepts the salute without keeping score.
after: {{other}} is delighted by your salute. The portrait accepts it with rather less need for encouragement.

before: You preserve your reputation for independence and make a rival. {{other}} finds the portrait’s visitors much easier to manage.
after: {{other}} becomes your rival. The portrait has acquired a considerably more agreeable social circle than its owner.

before: You pay for the work. Household shelter and food reserves improve, and {{other}} accepts a useful alteration to custom.
after: The stores are raised and the water kept out. {{other}} accepts a change in custom once custom has stopped smelling of wet grain.

before: You preserve your cash while the household loses stored food and wealth. The right to an empty cellar remains unimpaired.
after: You keep the money. The household keeps its ancient right to a cellar now occupied chiefly by water.

before: You gain Commons standing and lose favour with {{other}}. The household’s current stores are not miraculously moved by the petition.
after: The neighbours support the complaint. {{other}} asks whether the accumulated rights can also be expected to carry the buckets.

before: You improve the household’s shelter and keep the memorial on paper. {{other}} finds the living family’s gratitude less artistically satisfying.
after: The living household receives a better roof. {{other}} keeps the memorial drawing dry beneath it and finds the arrangement artistically disappointing.

before: You pay for the dedication and gain family reputation. Your existing rooms do not become drier because a mason spells your name correctly.
after: The dedication is paid for. A mason spells your name correctly while rain continues to have difficulty recognising it at home.

before: You preserve the coin and lose a little favour with {{other}}. The rain continues to make its own argument.
after: {{other}} leaves with both estimates. The rain submits its own argument without waiting for your patronage.

before: You improve Crown standing and make a rival of {{other}}. The funeral improvements are returned without comment.
after: You publish the offer and return the funeral improvements. {{other}} discovers how awkward it is to accuse a ruler of refusing a bribe.

before: You improve public order and Crown standing. {{other}} abandons the suggestion that your face could replace a metal.
after: The standard remains. {{other}} withdraws the suggestion that your face could be made to circulate in place of silver.

before: You spend twenty treasury gold on relief and improve food security. {{other}} sees money leave the account without becoming any lighter.
after: Twenty treasury gold buys relief. {{other}} watches the money leave without finding any opportunity to make it lighter.

before: You refuse the execution and improve public order. {{other}} loses trust in your willingness to make justice convenient.
after: The petition must wait for evidence. {{other}} is distressed to discover that the witnesses have been invited to contribute something.

before: You gain public wit and lose {{other}}’s affection. The argument is not improved by your willingness to test it.
after: {{other}} is asked whether the animal must swim before the classification takes effect. The argument becomes much less comfortable near the trough.

before: You keep your own observance and improve your relationship with {{other}} by declining to turn a meal into a trial.
after: You keep your own observance and let the meal remain a meal. {{other}} puts away a defence longer than the animal’s pedigree.

before: You refuse the ordeal, gain public standing and lose {{other}}’s favour. The oven remains available for bread.
after: You ask which part of the oven can identify a liar. {{other}} objects to your tone; the baker would like the bread space back.

before: You pay to have your objection heard through ordinary testimony. Crown standing improves without the heat being mistaken for evidence.
after: Your petition asks for ordinary testimony. {{other}} dislikes an objection that can be examined without warming the room.

before: You spend your strength rather than money and gain faith. {{other}} loses a customer but cannot lengthen your road.
after: You take the modest road yourself. {{other}} loses a customer and the power to add another mile whenever your purse is mentioned.

before: You improve Commons standing and make {{other}} a rival. The key’s owner learns that waiting can be recorded too.
after: You record the hungry households waiting outside. {{other}} discovers that a key can keep a door shut without keeping an account private.

before: You improve your household’s standing through the contribution and gain Church favour. The work is paid for by coin, without claiming an unbuilt roof has already risen.
after: Your contribution pays for the work. {{other}} records the coin, which has achieved rather more than the dry parchment did.

before: You gain wit and lose {{other}}’s patience. The book remains impressively dry.
after: You inspect the wonderfully dry record while the roof drips nearby. {{other}} finds your choice of comparison unhelpful.

before: You lose some strength to the detour and gain a little faith in the value of reaching your destination.
after: You arrive tired by the longer road. {{other}} cannot deny that the destination improves a pilgrimage considerably.

before: You improve public order by challenging the dangerous claim. {{other}} acquires a rival who knows exactly which boards are missing.
after: You point out the missing boards. {{other}} acquires a rival with a distressingly detailed knowledge of the miracle’s construction.

before: You improve public standing and lose {{other}}’s confidence in your willingness to make an example of someone.
after: The allegation is left out for want of evidence. {{other}} must deliver the moral point without the convenient pleasure of naming you.

before: You preserve the moral point and improve Church standing. {{other}} discovers that an argument can survive without a named victim.
after: The sermon keeps its argument and loses its named victim. {{other}} is disappointed by how well it still works.

before: You spend some strength and gain faith. {{other}} joins you after finding there is nobody left to applaud.
after: You take up the practical work. {{other}} joins you after discovering nobody is left to admire the refusal to speak.

before: You improve Church standing by declining to manufacture certainty. {{other}} is disappointed that the dog will not be treated as a witness for the defence.
after: You withdraw the claim. {{other}} regards the dog as a neglected witness for the defence, though it appears principally interested in the bone.

before: You spend the time securing the work and gain practical experience. {{other}} concedes that the blessing need not do every part of the job.
after: You fit the peg before climbing. {{other}} allows that a blessing need not be required to do the carpenter’s part as well.

before: You keep your health and lose a little favour with {{other}}. The peg remains admirably available.
after: {{other}} objects to your lack of confidence. The loose peg lies beside the platform, displaying admirable patience with both of you.

before: You improve public standing by challenging the claim. {{other}} learns that a polished spoon is not a testimonial.
after: You ask when the polished spoon last needed to recognise its family. {{other}} finds the demonstration less persuasive under questioning.

before: You lose health and the lung fever becomes more severe. {{other}} is impressed by an effort your body has not endorsed.
after: The effort worsens the fever. {{other}} praises your determination until asked whether determination will also lift you out of bed.

before: You spend strength on the safe route and lose some favour with the guide. The road continues to justify its existence.
after: You take the ordinary road. {{other}} calls it timid while walking over a surface that has the courtesy to remain underfoot.

before: You gain practical judgement and a little trust. {{other}} discovers that impatience is cheaper than a burn only until someone obeys it.
after: You wait for the safe handling. {{other}} concedes that impatience is cheaper than a burn only until somebody obeys it.

before: You pay for a safer arrangement and gain {{other}}’s respect. The ferryman reluctantly accepts that cargo can miss a crossing.
after: You pay to leave a bundle behind. The ferryman reluctantly accepts that cargo can survive the inconvenience of missing a crossing.

before: You pay for ordinary food rather than an exciting diagnosis. {{other}} accepts the loss of the herbs.
after: You buy ordinary food and discard the doubtful herbs. {{other}} laments a supper that will produce no medical discovery.

before: You pay for a useless tonic and lose a little health. No disease is removed, and the guarantee remains admirably difficult to invoke.
after: The tonic is useless and makes you feel worse. {{other}} points to the guarantee’s requirement that a deceased customer claim in person.

before: You gain a little performance at the cost of health and a fraud charge. The declaration has not repaired the body it describes.
after: The declaration reaches the employer before your strength does. The fraud complaint is much more capable of standing up than you are.

before: You preserve your life and gain public standing. {{other}} calls the crowd’s new distance a failure of confidence.
after: You step away and describe the danger. {{other}} calls the crowd’s increasing distance a disappointing failure of confidence.

before: You refuse the unsupported claim and improve your judgement. {{other}} is suddenly less certain which country contains the fortune.
after: You ask for the estate’s name before paying. {{other}} becomes less certain which country contains the fortune.

before: You gain judgement and a friendly bond with {{other}}. The little king is allowed to remain a piece of wood.
after: {{other}} shows you why the wooden king cannot simply order the board rearranged. You learn more than either of you intended about government.

before: You gain charm and make a rival of {{other}}, who did not intend the lesson to require a defence before witnesses.
after: Your comparison amuses the audience. {{other}} had not expected a wooden monarch to require a public defence.

before: You spend nine gold to help settle the dispute and improve public standing. The devil returns to work on unusually reasonable terms.
after: The devil is paid and returns to work. {{other}} finds nine gold a surprisingly efficient instrument of salvation.

before: You gain performance skill and help the show continue without claiming anyone has been paid. {{other}} discovers that goodness can be made to quarrel with itself.
after: You give the remaining virtues a quarrel among themselves. {{other}} discovers that goodness can fill an afternoon without paying a devil.

before: You gain a little wit and damage the acquaintance. {{other}} closes a gate that, for once, could not have kept you out.
after: {{other}} shuts the tiny gate. It is the first part of the castle that has actually managed to keep you out.

before: You gain understanding and a deeper bond. {{other}} eventually stops translating and asks for more bread.
after: {{other}} explains the word slowly, then stops translating and asks for more bread. You understand that part without help.
